body.statement: Under the stated four-sample design, \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}d_{\mathrm{BL}}(\mathcal L_P[\sqrt{n/L_n}(\widehat\tau-\tau(P))],N(0,V(P)))\to0\). Uniform map consistency and ass:lift-regularity imply that the half-open-cell lift branch is selected for both \(\widehat p\) and \(\widehat T\) with probability \(1-o(1)\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\); hence the measurable fallback has probability \(o(1)\) and does not alter the limit. This strictly extends the uniform-to-uniform, fixed-source dimension-two conclusion of Proposition 29 in ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT to general variable coefficients and to the four-input nested causal functional.
body.justification: The limit law turns the identified multivariate changes-in-changes map into an inferential object at the two-dimensional critical rate.
body.gap: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC stops at consistency, and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT explicitly leaves general-density dimension two open.
body.consumer: Applied researchers can attach uncertainty to the full-time versus part-time employment displacement vectors in a prespecified smooth Card--Krueger reanalysis.

obligation.what_is_open: Show that the nonlinear plug-in estimator is uniformly asymptotically equivalent to its oracle triangular-array linear score.
obligation.obstruction: The oracle Lindeberg calculation and deterministic bias arithmetic close, but neither implies the moving-pole score replacement nor the uniform quadratic nested remainder. Those are precisely the unresolved parts of oeq:uniform-critical-control.
obligation.attempted: The oracle summand envelope was compared with the normalization, and the bandwidth window was checked to imply Lindeberg negligibility; the available fixed-center argument cannot be promoted to a uniform random-pole expansion.
obligation.partial_result:
For the oracle linear term
\[
S_n=\sum_{g\in\mathcal G}\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i=1}^{n_g}\Psi_{g,h_n}(X_{g,i}),
\]
the smoothed Green envelope is \(O(h_n^{-1})\).  Hence every summand of \(\sqrt{n/L_n}S_n\) is
\[
O\!\left((n h_n^2L_n)^{-1/2}\right)=o(1),
\]
and the independent triangular-array Lindeberg condition follows because \(a_h<1/9<1/2\).  Conditional on the unresolved covariance convergence, this proves the Gaussian limit for the oracle linear term.  Lem:bandwidth-feasibility makes the order-minus-two bias negligible.  The missing steps are the uniform oracle-to-plug-in score replacement and the nonlinear nested remainder \(o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{L_n/n})\).
